identity.title: Effect of Y1Ste20 gene knockout on the mycelial morphology of Chaetomium globosum CGMCC 6882.

content.abstract: Chaetomium globosum CGMCC 6882 is an endophytic fungus isolated from Gynostemma pentaphyllum. However, its mycelia tend to intertwine and aggregate during submerged fermentation, eventually forming dense mycelial pellets. This phenomenon severely impedes diffusion and transfer of oxygen and nutrients from the fermentation broth to the interior of the mycelial pellets, thereby limiting the fermentation efficiency of C. globosum CGMCC 6882. To address this issue, a recombinant plasmid, pFC332-5 SrRNA-Ste20 gRNA, targeting the Y1Ste20 gene was constructed using CRISPR-Cas9 genome-editing technology. Subsequently, a Y1Ste20 gene knockout mutant, designated C. globosum XY1104, was successfully obtained through protoplast transformation, regeneration, and screening and identification. Results from solid dishes and liquid culture media investigations showed that C. globosum XY1104 exhibited a significantly lower mycelial growth rate than the parental strain, C. globosum CGMCC 6882. Moreover, its mycelia were shorter and more slender, and exhibited a denser distribution, with the formation of mycelial pellets completely eliminated. These findings demonstrate that Y1Ste20 is a key functional gene involved in regulating mycelial growth and morphological development in C. globosum and that targeted modification of this gene can be used to achieve morphological modification of fungus. Overall, this study provides reference for morphological regulation of other filamentous fungi.
